newsitem.title: INDIA: Duff & Phelps rates India forex obligations BBB-.
newsitem.headline: Duff & Phelps rates India forex obligations BBB-.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Company (DCR) said it has assigned a BBB- rating to the foreign currency obligations of the Republic of India, in its first rating of the country.

In a news release made available to Reuters on Tuesday, DCR said its investment grade rating reflects the Indian government's strong policy commitment toward establishing a competitive and creditworthy economy.
This commitment was reflected in the stabilisation and structual reforms implemented since the balance of payments crisis in 1991, DCR said.

Strong economic growth since 1993, falling inflation, an improvement in the balance of payments account, an unblemished debt service record and an improving trend in external debt indicators also supported the rating, it said.
DCR listed high fiscal deficits, infrastructural bottlenecks, slow progress on disinvestment of state-owned enterprises and high income inequality as reasons for not rating India higher.
But it added that while frequent changes in the government have caused uncertainty among international investors, the economic policy stance has shown little change.
